{#fy94} # Abstract

{#ml22} **Background: **Telomerase, by safeguarding damaged telomeres and bolstering DNA damage repair, has the capacity to heighten the radioresistance of tumour cells. Thus, in turn, can compromise the efficacy of radiotherapy (RT) and radioimmunotherapy. Our previous studies have revealed that the highly selective telomerase inhibitor, BIBR1532, possesses the potential to enhance the radiosensitivity of Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). In this study, we delve further into the impact of BIBR1532 on the immune activation induced by RT and elucidate the underlying mechanisms.

{#lgcc} **Methods: **Biological information analyses, immunofluorescence assays, western blot assays, flow cytometry analysis were conducted to elucidate the functions of the combination of BIBR1532 with radiotherapy in NSCLC. Intracellular levels of lipid peroxides, glutathione, malondialdehyde, and Fe<sup>2+</sup> were measured as indicators of ferroptosis status. Both in vitro and in vivo studies were conducted to examine the antitumor effects.

{#w7xu} IR induces telomere dysfunction, resulting in the fusion of chromosome ends, ultimately leading to a catastrophic failure in cell mitosis. ops.markdown: More significantly, our study explores how low-dose BIBR1532 combined with radiotherapy affects the TIME. BIBR1532 plus RT activates the cGAS/STING signalling pathway, whereas BIBR1532 alone does not. This synergy with IR may augment cGAS sensitivity to cytoplasmic dsDNA, possibly through BIBR1532-mediated effects on telomerase activity, since telomere shortening to a critical length entails a substantial time lag [@w:w24]. By contrast, IR induces exogenous DNA damage, directly causing chromosomal DNA breaks and generating substantial DSBs. The non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway then rapidly repairs these DSBs, but this template-free mechanism may inadvertently produce structurally aberrant chromosomal fragments that are improperly segregated into micronuclei [@w:w25]. Ruptured micronuclei release dsDNA into the cytoplasm, activating cGAS, which catalyses the synthesis of cyclic GMP-AMP (cGAMP) and triggers the innate immune response [@w:w26].
